question: How much energy does Vi - Hotheaded cost?
reframe: As the rules see it: what numeral sits in the Cost element of Vi - Hotheaded, and is that the whole price of playing her?

holding.line: Vi - Hotheaded costs 4 Energy, which is the numeral in her Cost element, and that is her whole play cost — the [2][R] on her is a separate activated ability, not part of playing her.

spans.text: the numeral in her Cost element
a separate activated ability, not part of playing her

notes.detail: Card data: Vi - Hotheaded — Energy 4, Might 3, Unit, Epic, Fury. The value itself is read off the card, not derived from a rule; the rules below say what that numeral means.
notes.if_false: If the printed numeral were anything other than 4 — a misprint, a reprint with a different cost, or stale card data — the answer changes outright. Nothing in the rules would flag it; check the physical card.

cites.quote: The numeral listed in the Cost element in the upper left corner of the card.

notes.claim: That numeral is where a Main Deck card's cost lives.

cites.quote: Main Deck cards have a Cost, listed in the upper left corner of the front face of the card.

notes.claim: The [2][R] printed on her is an activated ability's cost, paid only when that ability is used.
notes.detail: Her text reads "[2][R]: Double my Might this turn." The colon is what marks it: the cost before it belongs to the ability, so it is not added to the 4 Energy needed to play her.

cites.quote: Activated Abilities are recognized by the presence of a ":" in the text of the card, preceded by a cost and succeeded by an effect.

counterargument.reading: Her cost is 4 Energy plus [2][R], because both are printed on the card.
counterargument.why_it_loses: Only the Cost element is the card's cost. The [2][R] sits before a colon in her rules text, which marks it as the price of activating that ability while she is already on the board.

cites.quote: The numeral listed in the Cost element in the upper left corner of the card.

considered_rejected.why: Pay covers how a resource leaves the Rune Pool; the question is what the cost is, not how it is paid.
